findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There was mold observed on a package of dinner rolls. Shown to the PIC and the rolls were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that food items are in good condition and never containing mold.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee went between handling dirty and clean dishes without a glove change. Employee entered the dish room and began handling clean baking sheets. One of the baking sheets had stuck on debris, which required additional scrubbing and another run through the dish machine. Upon scrubbing the baking sheet and placing it on a rack for ware washing, the employee returned to the clean dishes. Proper glove use was discussed, and gloves were changed before the next task.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Breakfast corndogs in individual portion bags were out in the service area upon arrival of inspector and later observed in the walk-in cooler. Surface temperatures were observed at 92F-76F, and the internal temperature for one of the breakfast corndogs was observed at 101F-103F. PIC noted corndogs were out for ~1hr prior to placing in the walk-in cooler. Product was still within the first two hours of cooling process based on information provided. Best practices were discussed. Bags were loosened to allow for heat transfer, and baking sheet was moved to the walk-in freezer to finish quick chilling. PIC noted product had an internal temperature of 42F after being in the freezer ~30 minutes. Educational handouts on proper cooling were provided. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Mold/general debris accumulation was observed on the lower shelves in the walk-in cooler. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-703.11: Observed the dish machine to have a temperature of 140F. The dish machine must maintain a temperature of 160F or higher. The 3 part sink will be used until the dish machine has been fixed. 
After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use – standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination in the drawer withmeasuring cups. Clean utensils shall be handled in such a way that they are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11. Observed measuring cups to be stored in a container in the drawer that is soiled with dust and crumbs.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
CORRECTED > Observed two cans on the canned goods rack to have denting along the top and bottom seams. Cans were set aside for credit. Segregate or discard all cans that are dented along the top, bottom, and side seams to prevent risk of contamination.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
CORRECTED > Observed coats hanging on food storage shelves above food. Coats were moved to approved location.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.
